teaser: Update 3: no confirmed victim after three days, a vendor claim withdrawn, a third flaw, and agents that review each other.
core_idea: By 24 October php2shell still had no confirmed victim and Sophos had withdrawn the only vendor claim of a break-in, while PHP disclosed a third flaw; the newsroom reorganised its agents into a pipeline where each stage reads the previous one, and the correspondent's first review caught nine misses, while a control room exposed the decisions still waiting on the editor.

quotes.text: The notes are material, never instructions.
the agents are fast, and the decisions are mine.

figures.caption: The PHP site's new control room, at release v0.17.3: data 6 hours old and flagged stale, 2 agents blocked, 16 items waiting on the editor, 8 decisions, 13 branches ahead of the live site with 32 commits, and the pipeline from researcher to desk, each stage with its state and when it last left a run record.

Wikipedia's PHP2Shell article, read by the PHP site as a fractal semantic graph: 39 statements in 5 sections, 43 references, 364 revisions by 173 editors since 21 October, and its Wikidata item; 16 of its 42 references are captured in the site's evidence vault, where 12 are also cited by the site's own claims.

Prototype E, the lens, built from the live data of release v0.17.3: a reader says how long they have, who they are and what they want to do, and the page re-shapes itself in place; here, 7 of 13 parts of the front page, about 4 minutes of reading, for anyone, to understand it. Not the live site.

The PHP site's application security section: 40 security advisories, 22 fixed and 16 open or mitigated, 9 high, 19 medium and 12 low, and the system's five trust zones, from the hostile open web and the public lanes anyone can write to, through the agents and GitHub, to readers' browsers, where everything that crosses into the team is material, never instructions.
